202A.2 / CHAPTER 2 OF 11

Liquidity & price impact

How much does this order disturb the pool?

11 short chapters

01Price moves at the margin02Liquidity & price impact03Buy/sell pressure04Supply transfer05Early wallet flow06Demand acceleration07Attention conversion08Push, Hold or Fail09Meta saturation10Migration as event risk11PVP Dominance & Rotation

01Definition

Price impact is the change in execution price caused by your order relative to available liquidity.

02Why it matters

The same dollar order can produce very different fills in different pools.

03What to check

  • Current executable quote for the intended size
  • Pool depth and route
  • Impact, fees, and slippage tolerance separately

04Healthy / Dangerous

Healthy

The order fits the quote and the expected cost is understood.

Dangerous

Thin depth or broad tolerance turns a modest order into a poor fill.

05Beginner mistake

Expecting equal buy sizes to create equal moves.

06Takeaway

Thin liquidity magnifies each trade.

ILLUSTRATIVE · NOT A LIVE TOKEN

Go deeper

Price sensitivity is not automatically strength: it can amplify selling too. A ratio of price change to sampled net buying is descriptive, not a stable capital-efficiency score. Liquidity, routes, and missing trades can all change the comparison.
